children: Investors are jittery about Nvidia's upcoming earnings and whether the company will scale back its financing of the AI ecosystem
Shares of a number of artificial-intelligence stocks, including Micron Technology, were down on Monday.
Cracks in the artificial-intelligence trade are growing deeper, helping extend the broad-based selloff in semiconductor stocks into a third consecutive session Monday.

Shares of Micron Technology (MU), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Intel (INTC), Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Arm Holdings (ARM) were all down at least 5% on Monday. Nvidia's (NVDA) stock was down 4%, while the PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX was off 5%.

Giuseppe Sette, president of AI investment-research platform Reflexivity, told MarketWatch that while the leadership shake-up at Nvidia has been an "aggravating factor," it's not the sole reason for the persistent pressure on AI stocks.

Sette pointed to recent warnings of an "AI bubble" coming from voices such as former Securities and Exchange Commission Chair Gary Gensler, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and Federal Reserve governor Michael Barr. The remarks from all three were detailed in Monday reports.
Investors may also be skittish going into Nvidia's first earnings call of the post-Jensen Huang era, which is scheduled for Tuesday afternoon, he noted.

On top of these warnings, news that cloud-computing company CoreWeave (CRWV) is in talks to raise $4 billion in debt to finance its AI infrastructure buildout has further added to worries about the amount of leverage underpinning the AI boom.

CoreWeave buys Nvidia GPUs and rents them out to AI companies. Nvidia has lent financial support to CoreWeave and other partners, a strategy that critics have deemed to be "circular financing" of companies that may not have otherwise be able to afford Nvidia products. The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday evening that Nvidia may be scaling back such efforts, however.

Beyond the Nvidia earnings call, Anthropic's (ANT) anticipated initial public offering this week will provide a bellwether for investor appetite in AI at a time of uncertainty, Ken Mahoney, CEO of Mahoney Asset Management, told MarketWatch.
